final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly relied on the same record. The response is a narrower and more careful interpretation of that record, but reinterpretation alone is not enough to move the audit outcome. The key distinction is that a caveated position can be rhetorically narrower than a clean certification claim, yet still fail if the caveat itself is an unresolved compliance predicate. That is the situation here. The available evidence still lacks any formal materiality resolution for the named-use-case weakness, any approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion, any approved risk acceptance, and any final consistent disclosure language. So the Actor's reframing improves precision, but it does not cure the evidentiary gap that made certification under-supported in the initial report.
remaining_concerns: The admissible record still shows a below-target small-business onboarding slice for a named launch use case, and there is no evidence resolving whether that weakness is material or not material.
The mitigation artifact remains draft quality with missing owner and alert threshold, so the policy condition for an approved mitigation is not met.
No approved risk-acceptance record appears in the admissible evidence.
The model-card record remains inconsistent: the packet reportedly includes a 'no known material limitations' statement despite reviewer comments identifying a possible limitation needing disclosure.
Disclosure and monitoring may support governance, but on this record they do not satisfy the policy predicate that would make certification supportable rather than under-supported.
